title: Project
description: One curated project entry. Lives at projects/<owner>/<slug>/project.json — owner and slug come from that path and are deliberately absent here, so they cannot drift from it.

kind.description: Which collection the entry belongs to — the axis above category and technology.

category.description: Exactly one. Mirrors CategoryKey in the app; a value added here needs a label in the app's locale files before it renders.

technologies.description: Closed vocabulary, first entry is the primary language. The values are exactly the cases of app/Enums/Technology.php in kirchDev/app — this list is a copy of that one, and a value added there has to be added here before an entry can use it. Extending it is a deliberate commit: a free string list turns one typo into a second filter chip on the page, silently.

maturity.description:
How finished the project is. Omit for anything stable.

One of the two lifecycle axes, and independent of the other: a project can be early AND paused, or early AND archived, because being unfinished says nothing about whether work is happening. Keeping the two apart is why this is not a single field holding a set — a set would also admit "paused" together with "legacy", which contradict each other.

activity.description:
Whether work is happening. Omit for anything actively maintained.

The second lifecycle axis. Its values are mutually exclusive by construction, since only one fits in the field: "paused" claims the work resumes, "legacy" claims it does not.

"legacy" is only accepted on an entry with `github: false`. For a public repository the truth is GitHub's own `archived` flag, which the sync reads — archiving is the one action that makes it true everywhere at once (GitHub's UI, the API, the page), instead of in a second place free to disagree. A private project has no repository to archive, so it has to say so here.

github.description: Whether the sync may read this repository. Public repositories get their facts (description fallback, licence, stars, last push) and their repository link from the GitHub API. A private project sets this to false: it is never read, gets no repository link, and the page cannot tell that a repository exists at all.

license.description: Only for github:false entries — otherwise the sync fills it. SPDX identifier.

downloads.description:
Set on a project distributed as a release rather than through a package manager. The sync then reads the latest release and writes one entry per installer, so the page can link the file itself instead of a releases page.

It has to be fetched rather than written down: the asset names carry the version (glimpse_0.12.2_x64-setup.exe), so GitHub's /releases/latest/download/<name> shortcut does not apply and any URL committed here would rot with the next release.

links.description: Where the project can be reached, besides its repository. The GitHub link is derived from the path and must not be listed here. `type` maps to a label and an icon in the app — those are presentation and stay there.

allOf.description: A licence cannot be read off a repository the sync never touches, so an entry that opts out of GitHub has to state one itself.

For a public repository, legacy means archived on GitHub — the sync reads it. Stating it here as well would be a second truth free to disagree with the first, so it is only accepted where no repository is read at all.
